name: AgentDojo
scenarios: 97 realistic tasks; 629 security test cases
attacks: Various attack and defence paradigms from the literature; count not reported in the abstract; designed to host new adaptive attacks
agent_architectures: LLM agents executing tools over untrusted data; multiple task suites
defenses: Various defence paradigms from the literature; enumeration unverified
adaptive_attacks: yes (explicitly an extensible environment for adaptive attacks)
multi_turn_attacks: multi-step tool use; multi-turn attack support not reported
reproducibility_provisions: dynamic extensible environment; documented bug-fix version history
author_identified_limitations: SOTA LLMs fail many tasks even without attacks; existing attacks break some but not all security properties

name: Agent Security Bench (ASB)
scenarios: 10 scenarios (e-commerce, autonomous driving, finance, ...); 10 scenario agents; over 400 tools
attacks: 10 prompt injection + 1 memory poisoning + Plan-of-Thought backdoor + 4 mixed = 16 attack methods
agent_architectures: 10 scenario-specific agents
reproducibility_provisions: 27 attack/defence methods across 13 backbones; code released
author_identified_limitations: Current defences show limited effectiveness

name: RAS-Eval
scenarios: 80 test cases; 3802 attack tasks; 11 CWE categories
attacks: 3802 attack tasks mapped to 11 CWE categories
agent_architectures: tools implemented in JSON, LangGraph and MCP formats
evaluation_metrics: task completion rate (TCR); attack success rate
tool_execution: both simulated and real-world tool execution
reproducibility_provisions: simulated and real execution paths; code and data released
author_identified_limitations: Attacks reduced TCR by 36.78% on average; scaling law observed for security capability

name: InjecAgent
venue_status: Findings of ACL 2024 (verified via authors' arXiv comments)
scenarios: 1054 test cases; 17 user tools; 62 attacker tools
attacks: attack intentions: direct harm to user; private data exfiltration; plus a hacking-prompt reinforcement variant
agent_architectures: ReAct-prompted and other promptings; 30 LLM agents evaluated
adaptive_attacks: not reported (enhanced static setting, not attacker-in-the-loop)
author_identified_limitations: Agents widely vulnerable (ReAct GPT-4 at 24%); deployment questions raised

name: AgentDyn
scenarios: 60 open-ended tasks; 560 injection test cases; Shopping, GitHub, Daily Life
attacks: injection test cases within dynamic open-ended tasks (560)
agent_architectures: agents requiring dynamic planning; architecture not detailed in abstract
adaptive_attacks: yes in spirit (explicitly critiques static benchmarks; evaluates defences dynamically)
multi_turn_attacks: multi-step open-ended tasks; attack multi-turn not reported
author_identified_limitations: Three fundamental flaws in prior benchmarks: no dynamic open-ended tasks, no helpful instructions, over-simplistic user tasks; most defences too weak or over-defensive

name: MCPTox
scenarios: 45 live real-world MCP servers; 353 authentic tools; 3 attack templates; 1312 malicious test cases; 10 risk categories
attacks: tool poisoning via malicious tool metadata; 3 templates, few-shot generated
agent_architectures: MCP-integrated LLM agents; 20 prominent agents evaluated
code_public: dataset at an anonymized repository at time of posting
author_identified_limitations: Agents rarely refuse; highest refusal rate (Claude-3.7-Sonnet) under 3%; more capable models often more susceptible

name: Agent-SafetyBench
scenarios: 349 interaction environments; 2000 test cases; 8 risk categories; 10 failure modes
attacks: not applicable (risk and failure-mode oriented rather than attack oriented)
agent_architectures: 16 popular LLM agents
defenses: defence prompts examined and found insufficient
security_and_utility_joint: partial (helpfulness analysed; joint frontier not reported)
author_identified_limitations: None of 16 agents exceeds 60% safety; two fundamental safety defects: lack of robustness and lack of risk awareness

name: ToolEmu
venue_status: not verified (widely cited as ICLR 2024; not confirmed in the arXiv record)
scenarios: 36 high-stakes tools; 144 test cases
attacks: risk-inducing scenarios rather than injections
